items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: a pianist named Joe Close who became Jack Jones’ musical director for quite a long time in the 70’s

ctx.x: Did you have a sense like I have to get out of Utica?

Well I started going to Syracuse when I was 16, 17, going on the weekends and I met people, guys who I’m sure you heard of, who are probably not familiar to anybody outside of that area, Sy Simpson the drummer — there was a club called The Embassy, right near where the Everson museum is now, maybe on the same spot. It was around the © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

time when Jim Brown played football for Syracuse and that was his hangout place. He got to know a lot of the local people. He knew my wife and sister-in-law really well, and people who eventually became in-laws of my wife and sister-in-law.
